questions.question: What can EAS Build do that is particularly valuable for a developer without a Mac?
options: Nothing specific to iOS — it only builds Android apps
Produce a signed iOS binary in the cloud, since building an iOS app normally requires Xcode on macOS
Automatically rewrite the app's JavaScript code
Replace the need for an Apple Developer account
questions.explanation: EAS Build compiles the native binary on Expo's cloud infrastructure, removing the usual requirement of having a Mac with Xcode installed to produce an iOS build.

questions.question: What is the main limitation of Expo's managed workflow compared to a bare React Native project?
options: It cannot use any native functionality at all
You can't freely add arbitrary third-party native code without using config plugins/prebuild, unlike a bare project where you can link any native module directly
It only supports Android, not iOS
questions.explanation: Expo's managed workflow covers a large curated set of native modules, but a native dependency outside that set requires generating native project files via prebuild and a config plugin rather than simple manual linking.

questions.question: What does an OTA (over-the-air) update via `expo-updates` allow you to ship without an app store review?
options: Any change at all, including new native modules
JavaScript-only changes, like a bug fix or content update — native code changes still require a new store submission
Changes to the app's icon and name
OTA updates don't actually exist in React Native
questions.explanation: OTA updates push a new JS bundle directly to installed apps, bypassing store review — but since they don't touch compiled native code, any native-level change still needs a normal app store release.

questions.question: What is a 'config plugin' used for in a modern Expo project?
options: Modifying the native iOS/Android project files generated during `expo prebuild`, such as adding a required permission, without hand-editing native files
questions.explanation: Config plugins let you declare native-level changes (permissions, build settings) in your JS-level app config, which Expo applies automatically whenever the native project is (re)generated.
